planting.note: Plant rhizomes in late summer to early fall with the top surface exposed to the sun in well-drained soil so roots establish before frost.

directions: Set rhizomes horizontally with the top surface exposed to sun in well-drained soil in full sun; Butterscotch Kiss is a tall bearded iris hybridized by Gordon Plough from a cross of Cascade Splendor and Honeyflow with Twenty Grand, registered in 1955. It bears a glittery butterscotch-yellow self with heavily laced, ruffled edges and an orchid overlay that deepens toward the flower center, blooming on 36-inch stems in late midseason. It earned an Honorable Mention in 1957 and an Award of Merit in 1959 from the American Iris Society, and remained one of Plough's most sought-after introductions. Divide congested clumps every three to four years after bloom to maintain vigor.

directions: Set rhizomes horizontally with the top exposed in well-drained soil in full sun; Sugarplum Fairy is a tall bearded iris hybridized by Melba Hamblen from a cross of Touche and Misty Dawn with Potpourri, registered in 1979. Ruffled apricot standards flushed with pink open above violet falls edged in pink, with an orange-red beard, on well-branched 36-inch stems carrying up to eight buds. It received the Mission Bell Award in 1980 and an Honorable Mention in 1983 from the American Iris Society, and it later served as a parent of Frances Gaulter alongside Heavenly Harmony. Divide congested clumps every three to four years after bloom.

directions: Set rhizomes horizontally with the top exposed in well-drained soil in full sun; Heavenly Harmony is a tall bearded iris hybridized by Melba Hamblen from a cross of New Rochelle and Pretty Karen, registered in 1977. Pink standards flushed with violet at the base open above violet falls with pink hafts, set off by an orange-red beard, on 30-inch stems in late midseason. It received the Mission Bell Award in 1978 and an Honorable Mention in 1980 from the American Iris Society, and it later served as a parent of Frances Gaulter alongside Sugarplum Fairy. Divide congested clumps every three to four years after bloom to maintain vigor and flowering.
